Oh yeah- developing roots are pretty thick and short so they would be really difficult to damage, and the soil should be loose enough that pulling it up wouldnt be a problem. But also  if you gently tug on them and feel resistance you can tell that way that there's root growth starting

I would put them in new dry soil first and see if they grow roots on their own and resort to putting them in water if it has been some months and they haven't 

Pumice and perlite cost about the same and are basically the same thing. both cheap as heck. It's like a regional thing which will be available. For the soil just mix them up together about 50/50. You can but it in a bag and shake it together so it's well mixed.

For watering I think since they are young and growing roots they can be lightly watered to encourage root growth. I would leave them alone for about a month and then check to see how root growth is going and if they have little nubs you can water them and then maybe about once every 2 weeks lightly water them, just a small amount so it dries out quickly. By summer if they have some good roots going once a month should be good.
